name: East Face

approach_variants.name: The SR-20 pullout, over the rib south of the South Buttress into the basin east of the peak
approach_variants.notes: From the long pullout on the north side of SR-20 about a mile and a half west of Washington Pass, follow the cairned climbers' track from its east end down through timber, cross State Creek, and climb toward the basin below the south side of the peak. Six pitches, Grade III, first climbed in 1976. Note that this route is filed as northeast face while its name and aspect both say east.
hazards: Steep, loose scree chimneys directly below the wall that must be avoided rather than climbed
A descent by a different route than the one climbed, with no route-specific beta
A creek crossing and brushy climbers' path low down
No published marker at the base of the route itself
approach_variants.baseFinding: Traverse over the rib that extends south from the South Buttress into the basin east of Cutthroat Peak. That second basin is where the East Face routes begin. So the count is two basins, and the rib between them is the thing you cross: first the basin below the peak's south side, which is where the South Buttress and North Ridge parties go, then over a rib, then the east basin. If you have not crossed a rib, you are still in the south basin and you are under the wrong side of the mountain. The negative test against the North Ridge, which leaves the same boulder field: that route bears right and north into the basin beneath the North Ridge Notch, and gains it by a loose runout 5.7 pitch. If you are roping up for a single hard pitch to reach a notch, you are on the North Ridge, not on the East Face. A hazard that is also a route-finding instruction, and it is stated in both routes on this side: avoid the steep, loose scree chimneys directly below the wall on the way in. If your line into the base is up a confined chimney full of scree, you have picked the wrong way through and should back out and go round. There is no named crack or flake at the start: no per-route detail beyond this shared approach is published for this line, and the peak's other east-side route carries no marker either. What is recorded is the basin, the rib and the chimneys to avoid, and those are all real ground features. Descent: no route-specific beta exists beyond the general east-face pattern. Parties commonly descend the South Buttress with multiple rappels, or the West Ridge on fixed-anchor rappels plus downclimbing, rather than reversing the technical face.

waypoints.name: Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass, north side)
waypoints.note: No route-specific beta found under the exact name 'Northeast Face'; assumed to share the East Face/Cauthorn-Wilson approach via the same basin east of the peak
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to the long pullout on the north side of the road about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, roughly half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead. The climbers' track leaves the east end of the pullout. SR-20 over Washington Pass is closed in winter, typically from late fall until spring.

descent_text: No route-specific descent beta was found beyond the general East Face pattern: parties commonly descend the South Buttress (multiple rappels) or the West Ridge (fixed-anchor rappels plus downclimbing) rather than reversing the technical face.
